newsitem.title: UK: Ashanti sees cost cutting benefits in '98.
newsitem.headline: Ashanti sees cost cutting benefits in '98.

text.p: Ghana's Ashanti Goldfields said on Monday it expected the benefits from its cost-cutting programme to come through in 1998.
The programme includes renegotiations of supplies contracts, elimination of expensive contractors and "labour rationalisation".
A marked increase in operating costs at Ashanti's main Obuasi gold mine helped 1996 pre-tax profit fall to $60.1 million from $100.7 million.
To expand its production base, Ashanti is developing mining projects in Bibiani in Ghana and Siguiri in Guinea.
The Bibiani mine is expected to start production in the second half of 1998, while the Siguiri project is forecast to be completed by the end of next year.
"Bibiani and Siguiri will make a strong contribution to the Ashanti goal of becoming the premier gold mining group in Africa," Ashanti said in a statement accompanying its results.

The mining firm, in which British conglomerate Lonrho Plc has a 33 percent stake, said it aims to have a total of six operational mines by the end of 1998 after it boosted its presence across the African continent in 1996 through several acquisitions.
The group's exploration portfolio currently consists of 35 projects in 12 African countries.
"Obuasi's disappointing results nothwithstanding, Ashanti is well positioned to deliver on its promise of sustained growth in reserves, production and earnings," the Ghanaian mining firm said.
Gold production in 1996 rose to 1.02 million ounces compared with 0.94 million in 1995. The group has reserves and resources of more than 32 million ounces with over 21 million located at Obuasi.
